notes:
I couldn't write any notes because my research tools stopped working before I could read a single page.

My first step tried to open nine commentary pages at once: Enduring Word, the Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Wesley and Calvin pages on BibleHub, Precept Austin, and two of Chrysostom's sermons on 2 Corinthians on New Advent. That request failed with a "tool use limit exceeded" error. When I tried one page at a time, the fetch tool refused because it only opens addresses that have come up in an earlier search. Every search I then tried failed with the same limit error, so I think the limit for this session is used up.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to leave out what I couldn't find. Since I read nothing, that leaves nothing for any verse. Writing notes from memory and attaching URLs would break that rule and could misstate what those writers say, so I haven't done it.

To get the notes, you could start a new session and I'll run the research again, with fewer pages per step so the limit isn't hit. Or you could paste in the text of the pages you want used (for example the Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Precept Austin pages on 2 Corinthians 6). I would then write the verse-by-verse notes from that text only, with the URL for each point. In either case I plan to cover:
- **Traditional readings, verse by verse:** Enduring Word; Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub or StudyLight; Precept Austin.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** v. 1 ("receive God's grace in vain"), where Reformed and Wesleyan teachers disagree about whether grace can be lost, using Calvin and Wesley's own notes. Also vv. 14–18 ("unequally yoked"), on how far separation should go, using GotQuestions, Desiring God and The Gospel Coalition.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes, for example on "Belial" (v. 15) and the Old Testament passages quoted in vv. 16–18. Also Chrysostom's sermons on 2 Corinthians and Catholic Answers, plus any popular modern teaching on this chapter that the sites discuss.
